Those infernal orgies! That revelry is forward. Notice the unbroken silence aft! It seems to me a picture of life. Out in front, through the sparkling sea, shoots the gay, embattled, bantering bow — but only to drag dark Ahab after it, where he broods inside his cabin at the stern, built over the dead water of the wake, and further on, hunted by its wolfish gurglings. It is in an hour like this, with the soul beaten down and held to knowledge — as wild, untamed creatures are forced to feed — oh, life! It is now that I feel the hidden horror in you! items.new: For some time past, though only at intervals, the solitary, secluded White Whale had haunted those uncivilized seas mostly visited by the sperm whale hunters. But not all of them knew of his existence. Only a few, comparatively, had knowingly seen him, and the number who had actually and knowingly fought him was very small indeed. For many reasons — the large number of whale ships; the disorderly way they were scattered over the entire watery globe, many of them adventurously pushing their hunt along lonely latitudes, so that for a whole year or more at a stretch they might seldom or never meet a single sail of any sort that could tell them news; the extreme length of each voyage; the irregular times of sailing from home — all these, with other circumstances direct and indirect, had long prevented the specific news about Moby Dick as an individual from spreading through the whole worldwide whaling fleet. There could hardly be any doubt that several ships had reported encountering, at such and such a time or on such and such a meridian, a sperm whale of unusual size and malignity which, after doing great damage to its attackers, had completely escaped them; and to some minds, I say, it was not an unfair assumption that this whale must have been none other than Moby Dick. Yet since the sperm whale fishery had lately seen various and not infrequent instances of great ferocity, cunning, and malice in the whale under attack, those who by accident unknowingly fought Moby Dick were perhaps, for the most part, content to blame the peculiar terror he inspired more, as it were, on the dangers of the sperm whale fishery at large than on the individual cause. That, mostly, was how the disastrous encounter between Ahab and the whale had so far been popularly regarded.

items.new: Nor did wild rumors of all kinds fail to exaggerate the true accounts of these deadly encounters and make them still more horrifying. For not only do fantastic rumors naturally grow out of the very body of all surprising, terrible events, as a stricken tree gives birth to its fungi, but in life at sea, far more than on dry land, wild rumors abound wherever there is any adequate reality for them to cling to. And just as the sea surpasses the land in this respect, so the whale fishery surpasses every other kind of seafaring life in the wonder and fearfulness of the rumors that sometimes circulate there. For whalemen as a body are not exempt from the ignorance and superstition that all sailors inherit; but of all sailors, they are by far the most directly brought into contact with whatever is appallingly astonishing in the sea. Face to face they not only see its greatest marvels, but, hand to jaw, they fight them. Alone, in waters so remote that you could sail a thousand miles and pass a thousand shores without coming to a single chiseled hearthstone, or anything hospitable beneath that part of the sun — in such latitudes and longitudes, and pursuing such a calling as he does, the whaleman is wrapped in influences that all tend to make his imagination pregnant with many a mighty birth.

So in many cases he finally struck such a panic that, of those who had heard of the White Whale — through those rumors, at least — few of those hunters were willing to face the dangers of his jaw.

items.new: But there were still other, more vital practical influences at work. Even today, the original prestige of the sperm whale, as fearfully distinguished from all other species of leviathan, has not died out of the minds of whalemen as a body. There are those among them today who, though intelligent and brave enough to give battle to the Greenland or right whale, would perhaps — from lack of professional experience, or incompetence, or timidity — decline a contest with the sperm whale. At any rate, there are plenty of whalemen, especially among the whaling nations not sailing under the American flag, who have never met the sperm whale in battle, and whose only knowledge of the leviathan is limited to the ignoble monster originally hunted in the North. Seated on their hatches, these men will listen with a childlike fireside interest and awe to the wild, strange tales of southern whaling. And nowhere is the supreme tremendousness of the great sperm whale more deeply felt and understood than aboard the ships whose bows breast him.

items.new: And as if the now proven reality of his power had, in earlier legendary times, cast its shadow before it, we find some book naturalists — Olassen and Povelson — declaring the sperm whale not only to be a terror to every other creature in the sea but so incredibly ferocious as to be continually thirsting for human blood. Even as late as Cuvier's time, these or very similar impressions had not been erased. For in his Natural History, the Baron himself states that at the sight of the sperm whale, all fish (sharks included) are "struck with the most lively terrors," and "often in the precipitancy of their flight dash themselves against the rocks with such violence as to cause instantaneous death." And however much the general experience of the fishery may correct such reports, in their full terribleness — even down to Povelson's bloodthirsty detail — the superstitious belief in them is, in some turns of fortune in their calling, revived in the hunters' minds.

items.new: So, overawed by the rumors and portents concerning him, not a few of the fishermen recalled, in connection with Moby Dick, the earlier days of the sperm whale fishery, when it was often hard to persuade long-practiced right whalemen to embark on the perils of this new and daring warfare. Such men protested that although other leviathans might be pursued with hope of success, to chase and point a lance at such an apparition as the sperm whale was not for mortal man. To attempt it would inevitably mean being torn into a quick eternity. On this point, there are some remarkable documents that may be consulted.

items.new: Nor, credulous as such minds must have been, was this idea altogether without some faint show of superstitious probability. For since the secrets of the ocean currents have never yet been revealed, even to the most learned research, the hidden ways of the sperm whale beneath the surface remain, in great part, unaccountable to his pursuers. Various nations have in some way recognized a certain royal preeminence in this color. The barbaric, grand old kings of Pegu placed the title "Lord of the White Elephants" above all their other grandiloquent titles of dominion. The modern kings of Siam unfurled the same snow-white animal on their royal standard. The Hanoverian flag bore the single figure of a snow-white charger. The great Austrian Empire, Caesarian, heir to overlording Rome, took the same imperial hue for its imperial color. This preeminence applies to the human race itself, giving the white man ideal mastership over every dusky tribe. Beyond all this, whiteness has even been made a sign of gladness — among the Romans, a white stone marked a joyful day. In other human sympathies and symbols, this same color is made the emblem of many touching, noble things: the innocence of brides, the kindliness of old age. Among the Red Men of America, the gift of the white belt of wampum was the deepest pledge of honor. In many lands, whiteness represents the majesty of Justice in the judge's ermine, and adds to the daily grandeur of kings and queens drawn by milk-white steeds. Even in the higher mysteries of the most august religions, it has been made the symbol of divine spotlessness and power. The Persian fire worshippers held the white forked flame the holiest on the altar. In the Greek mythologies, great Jove himself was made incarnate in a snow-white bull. Among the noble Iroquois, the midwinter sacrifice of the sacred White Dog was by far the holiest festival of their theology — that spotless, faithful creature being held the purest envoy they could send to the Great Spirit with the yearly news of their own faithfulness. Directly from the Latin word for white, all Christian priests derive the name of one part of their sacred vestments — the alb, or tunic, worn beneath the cassock. In the Vision of St. John, white robes are given to the redeemed, and the twenty-four elders stand clothed in white before the great white throne, and the Holy One who sits there is white like wool. items.new: "Grin away. We'll see what turns up. Listen, Cabaco — there is somebody down in the after-hold who has not yet been seen on deck. And I suspect our old Mogul knows something about it too. I heard Stubb tell Flask, one morning watch, that there was something of that sort in the wind."
